findings.title: One-shot stdout writes refuse after emitting a partial success record
findings.description: A valid positive short count from os.write(1,line) raises STDOUT_WRITE. The selected file is removed correctly, but a success-record prefix remains in stdout; inspect has the same pattern. Error stderr writes also ignore short counts. This contradicts the literal no partial successful stdout contract and fails recoverable short writes.
findings.recommendation: Use a bounded write-all operation for recoverable short writes on stdout and stderr. Resolve the literal arbitrary-stream no-partial-on-failure promise explicitly: previously emitted stream bytes cannot generally be rolled back. Preserve nonzero failure, no accepted output and complete-record acceptance rules; do not silently weaken the frozen contract.
